title: Dashboard & Rollouts: Contrast, Keyboard Flow, and Locale-Ready Component Sweep
creator: Maya Chen
description: This ticket scopes a focused design sweep across the Console dashboards, rollout UI, and cost views to ensure WCAG-compliant contrast, robust keyboard navigation, and LTR/RTL & locale readiness for production rollouts. The goal is to produce updated component specs, prototypes, and acceptance criteria so engineers can ship consistent, testable changes: 1) fix low-contrast tokens in charts, pills, and inline copy; 2) formalize keyboard focus flow for the Rollout panel and cost filters (including skip links and clear focus indicators); 3) add ARIA semantics/announcements for rollout state transitions and cost updates; 4) verify formatting and layout resilience for translated strings and locale-specific number/date formats.
acceptance_criteria: All updated text colors achieve at least 4.5:1 contrast for body copy and 3:1 for large text per WCAG 2.1 AA; component tokens documented in Figma and a token migration guide provided.

Keyboard-only flow covers: global nav -> current route -> Rollouts drawer -> variant actions -> confirmation dialogs; tab order is linear and SHIFT+TAB reverses predictably; focus never becomes trapped unintentionally.
Rollout state changes (start/pause/rollback) send screen reader-friendly live region announcements (polite) and the semantic role of the Rollouts panel is defined with landmark/region attributes.
Cost view displays follow locale-aware number and currency formatting (CLDR) and maintain readable decimal/grouping separators for fr-FR, de-DE, ja-JP, ar-SA locales during testing.
Layout handles expanded translations: no truncation of critical labels, buttons keep minimum tappable area 44px, popovers adapt to RTL mirroring without overlay collisions.
Design tokens are added to Storybook with an accessibility knobs page; automated e2e tests (Cypress) added to verify keyboard flows and at least three locale snapshots per CI run.
Prototype (Figma) validated by at least one screen reader test using VoiceOver (macOS) and NVDA (Windows) with notes captured in comments.
Developer handoff includes component spec, CSS directionality guidance, a11y checklist, and suggested unit test cases for announcements and formatting.
No regression in existing rollout metrics dashboards; visual regression checklist created for color token swaps.
comments: 2026-02-12 Maya Chen: Initial research summary attached. Found 12 low-contrast token occurrences across Dashboard charts and 3 in the Rollouts drawer. Proposing a small palette refresh rather than redesigning charts.

2026-02-18 Liam O'Neill: Engineering feasibility reviewed. Keyboard trap in Rollouts caused by custom focus handler — ENG will prototype a fix that relies on native tab order and aria-activedescendant for variant lists. Adding ENG-4582 as a dependency.

2026-02-25 Priya Raman (PM): Prioritizing Rollouts keyboard flow and screen reader announcements as P1 because customers use rollouts in operational runbooks. Please add e2e test cases for announcement timing.

2026-03-03 Accessibility review (external consultant): VoiceOver test notes: announce 'Rollout started' only after the server confirms state; avoid splitting the message across multiple live region updates. Recommend 'polite' role and single composed string.
2026-03-10 Design review: Updated Figma frames with RTL mirroring and extended copy examples. Need to validate button min-widths with QA across languages with long compound nouns (de-DE).

2026-03-12 Liam O'Neill: Implemented CSS variables and Storybook tokens branch created. Engineering to run automated contrast scan (axe-core) in CI; requesting final sign-off on color choices from PM and Accessibility.
Next steps: schedule joint QA + design session (30m) to run manual screen reader checklist for rollouts and cost view; add locale snapshot jobs for fr-FR, ar-SA, ja-JP.
notes: This ticket aims to be a lightweight, targeted sweep — not a full visual redesign. Focus on semantic correctness, keyboard predictability, contrast fixes, and i18n resilience so that the next release ships accessible and locale-ready Console controls. Avoid changing core interaction patterns unless necessary for accessibility compliance.
